body:
Shadow (shadow@erols.com) wrote:

: Hal Merrill wrote:
: > 
: > There was a VERY interesting post on another newsgroup which copied
: > an article in one of the Baltimore newspapers.  I'll look it up if
: > anyone wants.  The article was about a well documented scientific
: > study of the results of drug testing in a hospital work environment
: > over several years.  Apparently those who tested positive were kept
: > on as employees.  The one big difference between those who tested
: > positive and those who tested negative is that the ones who tested
: > positive had a much higher rate of promotion in the workplace and
: > much better attendance record and were basically more productive
: > overall. 

: Wait a sec... the ones who tested positive were those who used drugs,
: and they had a better record?? Are you sure this is stated correctly?

I'd wager that it's because intelligent, educated individuals (which you
have to be, to work in a hospital) who use drugs are able to use them
without it adversely affecting their behaviour. They also would be able to
make intelligent decisions about drug use, since they would be in the
know about which drugs are dangerous and which drugs are harmless.

Thing I don't understand about that hair-sample drug test -- it seems to
be at least partially marketed towards parents. The thing I don't
understand is:

If the parents have such POOR parenting skills that they're completely
clueless to what their kids are getting into, so they need a drug testing
kit to tell if their kids are using drugs, then they obviously won't have
the parenting skills required to DEAL WITH the results of the drug test.

Oh well. It probably is primarily intended for employers to use on their
wage-slaves. I'm so happy that you Americans are coming up with such
useful inventions, for all the Fascists in the world to use on their
people.
